items.title: Putter Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 27, 2024
items.q: My wife’s father ... was in the same stables as Jack Dempsey

ctx.x: Yeah I was just imagining, you know my wife and I we have a little routine sort of when I get home from a gig she might say, “How’d it go?” Or the next morning if there was something of significance I might say, “Guess what happened last night.” So I’m envisioning the morning after that gig with Thelonious Monk where this guy comes up to you and makes this request.

Oh well that, it was months after the gig with Thelonious. It was months later. And I was coming home from a pretty stupid gig, which you know you work a number of them in the tuxedo at a country club with an accordion player, you know, like you’re feeding your family. And so I come home, it’s about 8:00 and my wife is standing at the door and she’s — my wife’s father and my wife passed away three years ago. My wife’s father © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

was a pugilist. He was a prizefighter and he was in the same stables as Jack Dempsey so he was really good. And his wife said, he says, “It’s either me or boxing. You have to give up boxing if you want me.” His wife. And so he gave up boxing. But he taught his daughter how to box. My wife. And she would, when she would get angry she would assume a pugilistic stance. You know? She just would get into that stance as if she was going to hit me.
